ctx context bundles for Omni Agent Handoff
description:
Make ctx the shared owner of context bundle format, storage, artifact management, OCR, and portable .ctx export for Omni Agent Handoff and future tools.

Design decisions:
- Bundle storage is central and app-independent, e.g. XDG data under ctx bundles, not inside Omni repos.
- Bundle id format: timestamp + short id + optional slug, e.g. 2026-06-24T10-41-03Z_7hf3k2_build-slides.
- Bundle lifecycle: draft -> sent -> archived/cancelled; collection creates draft immediately.
- Bundle item schema includes image, text, file, url, desktop_snapshot, handoff_record.
- .ctx archive is zipped portable form for remote/Oqto upload.
- File items support copied and referenced storage; target/export decides whether references must be materialized.
- OCR belongs in ctx; v1 can shell out to `ocrs` CLI as backend.

Acceptance / proof:
- ctx can create a bundle, add images/text/files/URLs/snapshots, run OCR for an image, export .ctx, and render agent-readable context.md.
- Schemas are generated/synced to ~/byteowlz/schemas.
- Existing ctx capture behavior continues to work.
- `cargo check` and relevant tests pass.

Overarching docs:
- Wiki design note: ~/wiki/projects/agent-handoff-context-bundles.md
- Omni coordination epic: ~/byteowlz/omni-vanilla trx-gbnd
- Schemas coordination issue: ~/byteowlz/schemas trx-8918
close_reason: Epic complete. ctx now owns the context bundle format, storage, artifact management, OCR, and portable .ctx export for Omni Agent Handoff. All three children (trx-1w8t.1 schema+sync, trx-1w8t.2 store+CLI+export, trx-1w8t.3 capture+OCR) are implemented and closed. Acceptance met: ctx can create a bundle, add images/text/files/URLs/snapshots, run OCR for an image, export .ctx, and render agent-readable context.md; schemas generated/synced to ~/byteowlz/schemas/ctx; existing capture behavior preserved; cargo check + 34 cargo tests + end-to-end CLI workflow + jsonschema validation all pass.

title: Define ctx bundle schema v1 and schema sync
description:
Define ctx bundle schema v1 in the ctx repo and generate/sync it to schemas.

Scope:
- Add JSON schema for bundle manifest with schema_version, id, timestamps, state, producer, items, warnings, handoff records.
- Item types: image, text, file, url, desktop_snapshot, handoff_record.
- Image item fields: role (screenshot/crop/pasted), path, mime, dimensions, source provenance, derived OCR references.
- Text item fields: role (task/note/clipboard/ocr/accessibility), path or inline text policy, source metadata.
- File item fields: copied/referenced storage, original_path, bundle path if copied, size/mime/hash if available.
- URL item fields: url, title, source app/window.
- Desktop snapshot item points to ctx.json or structured capture output.
- Handoff record shape should be queue-compatible: target_id, transport, bundle_id, status, timestamps, session_affinity_key, command/api metadata, output/log references.
- Include .ctx archive/export metadata and unresolved external references.

Acceptance / proof:
- Schema validates example bundles for a slide-building handoff and a generic Pi handoff.
- ctx repo has examples and tests or validation command.
- Copy/sync script publishes schema to ~/byteowlz/schemas/ctx/.
close_reason: Defined ctx bundle schema v1: added manifest.rs typed types (manifest, items image/text/file/url/desktop_snapshot, handoff records, warnings, export meta, unresolved refs) with RFC3339 timestamps; added examples/bundle.schema.json + slide-handoff.json + generic-pi-handoff.json validated via round-trip tests; extended config schema with bundle_dir and [ocr] section; updated and ran sync script, pushed ctx.config + ctx.bundle schemas to ~/byteowlz/schemas/ctx. cargo check + cargo test pass.

title: Add ctx bundle CLI commands for handoff workflows
description:
Add `ctx bundle ...` CLI commands for Agent Handoff integration.

Proposed command surface, designed to map to a future daemon/API:
- `ctx bundle create --producer omni --slug <slug> --json`
- `ctx bundle add-screenshot <bundle-id> --mode frontmost|display|all --json`
- `ctx bundle crop-image <bundle-id> --item <item-id> --rect x,y,w,h --json`
- `ctx bundle add-file <bundle-id> <path> --policy auto|copy|reference --json`
- `ctx bundle add-text <bundle-id> --role task|note|clipboard|ocr --file - --json`
- `ctx bundle add-url <bundle-id> --url <url> --title <title> --json`
- `ctx bundle add-snapshot <bundle-id> --json`
- `ctx bundle ocr <bundle-id> --item <item-id> --json`
- `ctx bundle handoff <bundle-id> --target <id> --status sent|failed|queued --json`
- `ctx bundle export <bundle-id> --format ctx --json`

Scope:
- Store bundles in configured central ctx bundle dir.
- Return stable machine-readable JSON for every command.
- Update bundle manifest and context.md atomically enough for UI use.
- Keep commands defensive: failed OCR/capture records warnings without corrupting bundle.

Acceptance / proof:
- A shell script can create a bundle, add a text task, add a file, add URL, export .ctx, and inspect valid JSON output.
- Commands have tests for id generation, manifest update, and context.md rendering.
- `cargo check` and `cargo test` pass.
close_reason: Added ctx bundle CLI commands and store. ctx-core/src/store.rs provides the central bundle store (XDG bundle_dir) with deterministic id generation (timestamp+shortid+slug), create/load/save, agent-readable context.md rendering, and item/handoff/warning helpers with 11 unit tests. ctx-cli/src/bundle.rs adds 'ctx bundle {create,add-screenshot,crop-image,add-file,add-text,add-url,add-snapshot,ocr,handoff,export,show,list}' all emitting stable JSON, defensively recording warnings instead of corrupting bundles. ctx-core/src/export.rs exports portable .ctx zip archives that materialize referenced files and record unresolved refs + export metadata. Proof: shell script creates a bundle, adds text task+file+URL, records a handoff, exports .ctx, and the resulting manifest validates against ctx.bundle.schema.json (verified with jsonschema Draft7). cargo check + cargo test (34 tests) pass; existing capture behavior unchanged.

title: Add macOS capture, crop, and OCR bundle backend
description:
Implement ctx capture/crop/OCR backend for macOS-first Agent Handoff.

Scope:
- Add screenshot capture modes needed by Omni: frontmost window, current display, all displays placeholder/future.
- For region crop workflow, capture current display image and crop an existing image by rectangle.
- Record best-effort provenance: app, window title, URL if provided by Omni, display, mode, rect, timestamp.
- OCR backend belongs in ctx. First backend may shell out to `ocrs` CLI; make command configurable.
- Default policy for Agent Handoff: OCR crops automatically, full screenshots optional/configurable.
- Fail gracefully when permissions or OCR engine are missing; record warnings and actionable error messages.
- Keep design open for Wayland portal capture and Windows later.

Acceptance / proof:
- On macOS, ctx can add a frontmost-window screenshot item to a bundle.
- ctx can crop an image by x/y/w/h and add the crop as a new image item.
- ctx can run OCR on the crop using configured `ocrs` command and write `ocr/<item>.txt` or equivalent.
- Permission/OCR failure paths produce structured JSON errors/warnings.
- `cargo check` and `cargo test` pass.
close_reason: Added macOS capture/crop/OCR bundle backend. ctx-core/src/bundle_capture.rs implements capture modes frontmost (focused window, cropped from its display via x_win), display (main display), and all (every display) with best-effort provenance (app, window title, url, display, mode, rect, timestamp). crop_image crops by x/y/w/h and validates bounds. OCR backend shells out to the configurable command (default ocrs) and attaches OCR text items; permission/engine failures and missing images degrade to structured 'ocr_failed' warnings (4 unit tests cover the graceful paths). OCR command is configurable via [ocr] in config.toml. Design leaves room for Wayland portal / Windows capture later. cargo check + cargo test pass.

title: Implement active app/window capture adapters (macOS/Windows/Linux)
Screenshot context ingestion (app/window/url) across platforms
Capture selected text as privacy-sensitive current context
description:
## Problem

ctx captures active application/window/browser/terminal context, but it cannot expose the text the user has deliberately selected. Voice-command and agent clients therefore cannot implement commands such as “rewrite this,” “explain this,” or “send this to …” without independently querying platform accessibility interfaces.

Selected text is substantially more sensitive than ordinary app/window metadata. Capture must be explicit, bounded, freshness-correlated, and safe around secure controls.

## Goal

Add optional structured selected-text capture, beginning with macOS Accessibility/AX, behind the existing provider seam. Unsupported platforms, missing permissions, unsupported controls, timeouts, and empty selections must degrade gracefully without failing the rest of a context capture.

Support both consumers of full `ctx --json` captures and clients using lightweight `ctx current --json`. Decide and document whether selected text belongs in the existing current-context schema, requires a schema revision, or is supplied as a privacy-sensitive correlated payload. Do not silently add an unbounded sensitive field to default reports.

## Requirements

- Add an explicit opt-in/configuration control for selected-text capture; default behavior must be privacy-preserving.
- Implement macOS capture through Accessibility/AX using the focused UI element and selected-text attributes where supported.
- Preserve selected text exactly, including multiline Unicode and whitespace.
- Never emit selected text in diagnostic, debug, trace, or error logs.
- Use a bounded timeout and ensure selection capture cannot stall an otherwise successful context capture.
- Represent outcomes sufficiently to distinguish:
  - captured selection,
  - no active selection,
  - unsupported application/control,
  - accessibility permission denied,
  - timeout/failure.
- Correlate the result with app, bundle ID, window, and/or current-context sequence so consumers can reject stale text after focus changes.
- Revalidate focus/freshness before publishing where practical; never retain a previous selection after the active context changes.
- Explicitly exclude secure/password fields. Investigate and document behavior for browser contenteditable fields and other controls that do not expose standard AX selected-text attributes.
- Preserve the existing host/provider abstraction and graceful behavior on unsupported operating systems.
- Consider configurable size limits and explicit truncation metadata so large selections cannot create unbounded context payloads.
- Update generated JSON schema, example configuration, README/help, and current-context schema documentation as required.
- Keep examples generic and free of third-party internal data.

## Suggested interface considerations

A successful payload should be structured rather than an ambiguous nullable string, for example with status, text, truncation, capture timestamp, and context sequence/source metadata. The implementation may choose a different shape if it preserves the outcome and freshness semantics above.

The full-capture path and lightweight current-context path should share one normalized representation rather than defining incompatible selected-text formats.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selected-text capture is opt-in and disabled by default, or an alternative privacy design is explicitly justified and documented.
- [ ] On macOS with Accessibility permission, selecting multiline Unicode text in a normal editable text field produces JSON containing exactly that selection.
- [ ] With no selection, output reports an empty/no-selection outcome and never repeats a previous selection.
- [ ] With Accessibility permission denied, ctx still returns the remaining context and reports graceful unavailability rather than failing the command.
- [ ] Unsupported controls and secure/password fields do not expose their contents.
- [ ] Capture obeys a bounded timeout and stale results are not associated with a newer app/window/current-context sequence.
- [ ] Browser contenteditable behavior is tested or documented as unsupported with a clear outcome.
- [ ] Unit tests cover configuration defaults, schema serialization, status variants, Unicode/multiline preservation, truncation if implemented, and stale-result/focus-change handling using a fake provider.
- [ ] Platform-gated tests or a documented manual proof exercise the macOS AX adapter.
- [ ] README/config examples and generated JSON schemas are updated.

## Proof of positive outcome

Run the repository-standard validation:

```bash
just generate-config
cargo fmt --check
cargo check --workspace
cargo test --workspace
```

Manual macOS proof:

1. Enable the selected-text capture option and grant ctx Accessibility permission.
2. Select a known multiline Unicode fixture such as:

   ```text
   First line
   Grüße — 東京
   ```

3. Run the documented full-capture command and `ctx current --json`; show that the structured JSON preserves the selection exactly and includes freshness correlation.
4. Clear the selection and repeat; show a no-selection outcome with no stale text.
5. Change focus between two applications during or immediately after capture; show that stale text is discarded or marked invalid rather than attached to the new context.
6. Revoke Accessibility permission and repeat; show that app/window context still succeeds while selection reports permission denial/unavailability.
7. Select text in a secure/password field; show that no sensitive value is returned.
8. Test a browser contenteditable field and record the supported result or documented unsupported status.
9. Inspect logs produced during the above steps and verify none contain the selected fixture text.

title: Add neutral deliberate Bundle handoff to external destinations
description:
## Outcome

Enable a person to deliberately send or stage a reviewed `.ctx` Bundle, with an optional instruction, to an external destination without coupling ctx-core to Oqto or any other agent host. ctx owns capture, Bundle review/export, neutral handoff values, and a small destination seam. Each integration owns authentication, target discovery, upload, prompt/message semantics, and target-specific identifiers. Start with the simplest sufficient API; MCP remains an optional resource/pull surface through ctx-mcp, not a required transport for push handoff.

## Domain constraints

- Current Context is lightweight device-local state and MUST NOT trigger network calls, uploads, prompt submission, or model-context injection.
- Only an explicit user action may create a Handoff from a reviewed Bundle.
- Target identifiers and remote references are opaque to ctx; no Oqto Account, Session, work-directory, Runner, placement, or other target-domain types enter ctx-core.
- A Handoff distinguishes at least `stage` and `send` modes when the destination supports them, and unsupported modes fail explicitly.
- Destination implementations may use a simple HTTP API, an existing SDK/CLI, MCP, or another transport; the domain contract must not require one. Do not invent a new wire protocol or adapter framework until a concrete second implementation proves the need.
- Credentials remain owned by the destination integration and must not be persisted in Bundle manifests or receipts.

## Candidate neutral values

- `DestinationTarget`: opaque id/URI plus human-readable title/description.
- `HandoffRequest`: request/idempotency id, pinned Bundle id/hash/archive, optional instruction, opaque target, requested mode, and source provenance.
- `HandoffReceipt`: staged/sent/rejected status, opaque remote references, target display data, warnings, and retry-safe correlation.
- A minimal destination interface should be explored around `list_targets(query, current_context_hints)` and `handoff(request)`; keep it deep and avoid leaking target-specific methods.

## UX requirements

- CLI/Overlay flow is Capture/choose existing Bundle -> review/redact -> choose destination/target -> add instruction -> stage/send -> show receipt.
- cwd/project/app/URL from Current Context may be passed as neutral target-suggestion hints. Ambiguous resolution MUST present choices or fail; never silently guess.
- Preview is the default. Noninteractive confirmation is allowed only through an explicit flag and must remain auditable.
- Offline, unauthorized, oversized, unsupported-content, duplicate/retry, and ambiguous-target outcomes are legible and preserve the local Bundle.

## Proof of positive outcome

1. Unit/schema tests round-trip neutral targets, requests, receipts, modes, opaque references, provenance, and structured errors.
2. A fake destination proves ctx-core has no dependency on any product integration and demonstrates target discovery plus stage/send receipts.
3. A CLI integration test sends a self-contained test Bundle through the seam after explicit confirmation and prints stable JSON receipt output.
4. Tests prove `ctx current`, focus reports, screenshot watching, and Bundle creation alone perform no handoff/network/model action.
5. Retrying with the same idempotency identity does not create an unbounded duplicate handoff in the fake implementation.
6. Ambiguous target hints return explicit choices; unavailable/denied targets never fall back to another destination.
7. Bundle consent/redaction rules for clipboard, selections, screenshots, page text, and local paths survive handoff unchanged.
8. A conformance fixture is sufficient for an external repository to implement an Oqto or other destination without importing target concepts into ctx-core.

## Boundaries

- No Oqto implementation in this issue; track that in Oqto.
- No automatic context injection or ambient event-driven sends.
- No requirement to expose ctx-mcp publicly or make device-local resources remotely reachable.
- No package registry or generalized plugin runtime.
- Do not replace `.ctx` archive export, which remains the universal manual fallback.

Split implementation children only after the neutral contract and first real destination reveal actual seams.

Implement ctx-mcp as a neutral read-only context Resource server
description:
## Outcome

Turn the existing stub `ctx-mcp` crate into a target-neutral, read-only MCP Resource server for deliberate access to ctx Current Context and durable Bundles. MCP-capable agent hosts can discover and read context without importing ctx libraries or receiving automatic prompt injection. Implement against MCP 2026-07-28 semantics where supported, while isolating the wire adapter from ctx-core so protocol evolution does not change ctx's domain model.

## Resource model

Expose stable custom-scheme resources such as:

- `ctx://devices/<device-id>/current` — the complete lightweight Current Context snapshot with sequence and updated time;
- `ctx://bundles/<bundle-id>` — Bundle summary/manifest resource;
- `ctx://bundles/<bundle-id>/items/<item-id>` — one Bundle item/capture and its provenance;
- parameterized templates for Bundle/item lookup where useful.

Exact URI paths must be versioned and traversal-safe. Local filesystem paths are implementation details and must not become remote resource identity.

## Behavioral constraints

- Resource discovery/read is pull-only. Listing, subscribing, focus changes, screenshot detection, or Bundle creation MUST NOT inject model context, send messages, invoke tools, or call an AI provider.
- The MCP client/host decides whether a selected resource enters a prompt. ctx supplies resources, annotations, provenance, and structured unavailable outcomes only.
- `ctx://.../current` returns the complete replace-whole Current Context state, not a reconstruction from an event stream. A change notification is only an invalidation hint; consumers re-read the snapshot.
- Bundle resources pin existing durable Bundle contents and preserve their consent/redaction/provenance metadata.
- Clipboard, Selection, Screenshot, Page Text, and accessibility data remain unavailable when disabled/denied; ctx-mcp must not bypass capture policy or silently substitute stale content.
- Large binary items use bounded reads or resource links rather than uncontrolled base64/context expansion. Results advertise MIME type and size where known.
- Stdio/local operation is the safe default. Any Streamable HTTP mode is separately configured, authenticated, bounded, and disabled by default; never expose desktop context on a network listener implicitly.
- ctx-mcp knows no Oqto, Pi, Claude, Account, Session, Agent, work-directory, or destination concepts.
- Handoff/stage/send remains tracked separately by `trx-h3q2`; this issue does not add destination APIs or a target adapter framework.

## MCP surface

At minimum implement and test:

- `server/discover` and version/capability reporting;
- `resources/list` with deterministic ordering, pagination, TTL, and private cache scope;
- `resources/templates/list` where parameterized resources are useful;
- `resources/read` with text/binary/resource-link handling and precise missing/denied/unavailable errors;
- `subscriptions/listen` for explicit Current Context/Bundle invalidation subscriptions if the selected SDK supports the 2026-07-28 contract cleanly; otherwise document and defer subscriptions rather than inventing a parallel bus.

Do not expose every Bundle operation as an MCP tool. Add a tool only when a concrete model-controlled action cannot be represented as resource selection/read and has explicit consent semantics.

## Proof of positive outcome

1. MCP conformance/integration tests start `ctx-mcp` over stdio, call discovery, list resources, read Current Context, read a Bundle summary, and read text plus image items.
2. A generic MCP test client consumes the server without target-specific code; no Oqto dependency appears in ctx-core or ctx-mcp.
3. Listing and reading are deterministic, paginated, bounded, traversal-safe, and return private cache metadata where applicable.
4. Tests prove disabled clipboard/screenshot/selection capture cannot be recovered through MCP, malformed Bundle manifests cannot escape the Bundle root, and missing/denied resources return structured errors.
5. Updating Current Context increments its sequence; an opted-in subscriber receives only an invalidation and must re-read the complete snapshot. With no subscription, no unsolicited context is delivered.
6. Creating/focusing/reporting context while no MCP read occurs causes zero model, network, handoff, or destination activity.
7. A large image Bundle item does not force its bytes into a textual model response; the host can retrieve it as typed resource content under configured limits.
8. Network exposure tests prove HTTP is off by default and an unauthenticated remote request cannot read any resource when HTTP is enabled.
9. README documents explicit host configuration, privacy expectations, resource URIs, and the distinction between resource availability and prompt inclusion.

## Boundaries

- No automatic prompt attachment or `ui/update-model-context` behavior.
- No Bundle push/destination integration; see `trx-h3q2`.
- No generalized event bus.
- No remote synchronization of device-local Current Context.
- No target-specific authentication or identifiers.

Handle nested multiplexers (herdr inside tmux/zellij) in current-context reporting
description: When herdr runs inside a tmux or zellij pane, both the outer and inner multiplexer hooks fire and last-writer-wins on the state file gives ambiguous/racy results. The innermost multiplexer holds the real context (cwd, project, agent), but outer focus changes are still meaningful signals. Options: reporters include a nesting depth/parent-source field so ctx can prefer the deepest active reporter; or inner reporters detect $TMUX/$ZELLIJ and claim precedence; or outer hooks suppress reporting when the focused pane runs a nested multiplexer. Depends on trx-p9k5 and trx-e20z.
close_reason: Added depth field to reports/state with 2s nested-report grace window preferring deepest reporter; tmux hooks skip panes running nested multiplexers
